discovery: Prediction and discovery of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and its correlated and superconducting flat-band phases

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University / Applied Materials, Israel

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials and strongly correlated electrons
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this with a tear-and-stack technique and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, all tunable in a single device by gate voltage. This tight loop between theory and experiment launched moiré quantum matter, a new field. It now includes orbital ferromagnetism, Chern insulators, Wigner crystals, and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted materials. Many laboratories worldwide, including through local spectroscopic imaging, have reproduced and extended these phases. Twist angle has become a design parameter for strongly correlated and topological states of matter. Few discoveries of the past decade have changed condensed matter physics so deeply or opened so many directions.
